summary: the cases of the crash, reset and shutdown suites on i686, against kernels that never reset, power off for a halt, and reset after one

argv: ARCH=i686 sh tests/proofs/guest.sh make rach2 && ARCH=i686 sh tests/proofs/guest.sh copy ${WORK} rach2/kernel
ARCH=i686 RACH2_WORKERS=4 exec tests/run crash reset shutdown

faults.name: no-pulse
faults.summary: a missing event: the keyboard controller's pulse is never sent, so a machine with the earlier mechanisms left out never resets

faults.name: halt-powers-off
faults.summary: an unexpected exit and a lost transport: a halt powers the machine off, so QEMU ends and its console closes before it says that the machine halted

faults.name: halt-resets
faults.summary: a wrong end: the machine resets once it has said that it halted, so its processors run again where the case expects them halted
